newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty takes rest after days of NBP interventions.
newsitem.headline: Zloty takes rest after days of NBP interventions.

text.p: The Polish zloty, groggy from five days of central bank punishment, barely moved against the basket of currencies on Thursday taking a breather before next week when dealers saw more central bank action coming its way.

"Today was completely different than the last five days -- nothing happened on the market and the zloty barely moved. But we are likely to see action again on Monday as foreigners come to buy Polish T-bills," said Pawel Gajewski of Creditanstalt.
The zloty closed flat at 2.50/2.46 percent from the trading band centre at 3.1480/95 to the dollar, down from 3.1415/25 on Wednesday and at 1.8315/25 to the mark, flat from 1.8320/28.
The NBP said yesterday it wanted to see the zloty no higher than 2.5 percvent from the parity rate and the market complied.
"It seems both the market and the National Bank of Poland became finally tired of constant battling, but the zloty may gather new strength next week," said Piotr Mielusz, forex dealer at PBR SA.

Over the last five days the zloty's upward stabs were mainly fuelled by foreign purchases of treasuries on the primary and secondary markets as good fundamentals made Polish paper attractive. The treasury is offering 1.3 billion zlots worth of T-bills on Monday.
On the money market overnight rates fell to 19.0/19.5 percent from 19.8/20.4 percent at the opening despite a 276 million zloty sale of 91-day NBP-bills with an overnight value date.
The average yield of the 91-day rose to 22.20 percent from 22.19 percent on Wednesday.
Tomorrow/next rates also eased to 19.2/20.2 percent from 19.9/20.8 percent despite a 1.2 billion zloty 14-day reverse repo, which kept the maximum rate at 22.15 percent.
"The market is highly liquid becuase of all the cash created by central bank interventions on the forex market over the last five days," one dealer at a Polish bank said.
